data.body:
Resolved. Re-verified both sites on current origin/main (4034e96388, after 01e8 closed) — 01e8 did NOT rewrite either call, so both were still unbounded. Bounded them by call profile per the ticket's cited precedent:

1. _commands/init.py fetch <remote> <branch> (the cold first fetch of the tickets branch into a fresh store) -> new _git_fetch helper, _FETCH_TIMEOUT=300, matching the _snapshot/repo_snapshot cold-materialize precedent (bug 747f). On timeout it returns a synthetic CompletedProcess(124) naming the op+bound; the mount site now surfaces an actionable WARNING and proceeds off the existing tracking ref (non-fatal — sync self-heals), never a bare TimeoutExpired or hang.
2. _commands/fsck_repair.py push origin HEAD:tickets (incremental a3-remediation push against a warm clone) -> new _git_push helper, _PUSH_TIMEOUT=30, matching the _store/push.py precedent. The synthetic 124 flows into the existing 'ABORT: push failed for batch N: <stderr>' path, so the descriptive timeout message surfaces there.

AC1 (explicit timeout + justifying comment): done, both sites. AC2 (actionable error naming op+bound, never bare TimeoutExpired/hang): done via the CompletedProcess(124) precedent. AC3 (held-out RED->GREEN): tests/unit/test_git_timeout_bounds_983f.py — 7 tests: precedent-constant equality, timeout-is-passed (spy), TimeoutExpired-folds-to-descriptive-124 for each site, plus a wiring test that the remote-mount arm fetches through the bounded helper. AC4: make lint + make typecheck clean; init.py 724 / fsck_repair.py 381 LOC (<800); related suites green (the one batch failure was cross-file sys.path pollution of rebar_reconciler, passes in isolation). Landing via Gerrit.
